title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (2026)
author: Sofia Patel
summary: Canonical People Ops playbook covering end-to-end hiring, structured onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle for managers at Redwood Inference.
body:
Purpose

This document is the canonical People Operations playbook for hiring, onboarding, performance reviews, and manager responsibilities at Redwood Inference. It consolidates approved processes, templates, timelines, and SLAs that apply to all teams unless a business unit-approved exception exists (see related_pages).

Owners and escalation

- Document owner: People Ops (Sofia Patel)
- HR business partner: assigned per department (see team directory)
- Escalation: people-ops@redwood.com -> Head of People Ops (Priya Rao)

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Overview: Our hiring process balances speed, candidate experience, and consistent skill assessment. Typical time-to-offer target: 28 calendar days from requisition approval to verbal offer. Time-to-fill SLA for critical roles (engineering, infra, security): 45 days.

Key stages (use the Recruiting ATS to track):

1. Requisition & approval
   - Manager raises requisition in Greenhouse with role profile, justification, and proposed IC/manager level.
   - People Ops approves budget and JD within 3 business days.
2. Sourcing & outreach
   - Sourcing lead posts to agreed channels and runs targeted sourcing for priority roles.
   - Passive outreach templates are centrally maintained; personalize where appropriate.
3. Phone screen (recruiter)
   - 30-minute screen to confirm interest, compensation expectations, right-to-work, and basic role fit.
   - Recruiter completes ATS scorecard: must pass to advance.
4. Technical/Role interviews
   - Structured interview loop defined per role type (templates below). Interviewers must use standardized rubrics.
5. Onsite / Final (virtual or in-person)
   - Final panel + hiring manager + peer. Offer committee reviews for calibration on salary band and level.
6. Offer & close
   - People Ops drafts offer within 48 hours of verbal approval. Target to deliver written offer within 5 business days of final interview.

Interview panel requirements and diversity best practices:

- All panels must include at least two interviewers and represent different functions if possible (e.g., a peer and a cross-functional collaborator).
- Include at least one trained interviewer who has completed Redwood's interviewer training in the last 18 months.
- For senior roles (L4+), include a cross-team stakeholder.
- Use structured rubrics; avoid questions about protected characteristics. People Ops provides interview training and anti-bias resources.

Standard scorecard attributes (example):

| Attribute | Description | Rating (1-5) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Role competence | Domain-specific skills, system design or coding |  |
| Problem solving | Approaches ambiguity, tradeoffs, alternatives |  |
| Collaboration | Communication, stakeholder management |  |
| Culture add | Alignment with Redwood values and team norms |  |
| Overall recommendation | Hire / No hire / Hire with reservations |  |

Offer approvals and bands:

- Compensation bands are maintained by Finance + People Ops and updated quarterly.
- All offers outside band or with sign-on bonuses require Director-level sign-off and legal review for candidates in restricted jurisdictions.

2) Candidate experience & compliance checklist

- Recruiter must send confirmation email after each interview step with next steps and timelines (template in ATS).
- Background checks: initiated after acceptance; role-dependent (required for Dedicated & Private deployment customer-facing roles).
- Data handling: candidate PII is retained per our data-retention policy in security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.

3) Onboarding: 1st day to 90 days

Goal: get new hires to productive independence while signaling belonging and psychological safety. People Ops and hiring manager co-own onboarding delivery.

New hire timeline (minimum recommended checkpoints):

Day 0 (pre-boarding):
- IT provisioning request submitted 5 business days before start (email: it-ops@redwood.com).
- Welcome packet and first-week agenda sent.

Day 1:
- HR welcome + benefits orientation (60m).
- Manager 1:1 to set expectations and 30/60/90 goals (30m).
- Team meet-and-greet + assigned buddy.

Week 1:
- Technical environment access validated (repos, corp VPN, internal docs).
- Role-specific onboarding plan reviewed with manager.
- Buddy check-ins daily.

Week 2-4:
- First deliverable assigned (small scoped ticket or doc) to validate setup and introduce code/review norms.
- Scheduled learning path (internal training modules + product demos).

Day 30: Manager + new hire checkpoint (structured feedback form).
Day 60: Midpoint adoption check (progress vs 30/60/90 goals).
Day 90: Formal onboarding review and potential conversion for contractors/interns.

New hire checklist (table):

| Item | Owner | Success criteria |
|---|---|---:|
| IT account & laptop | IT Ops | Laptop delivered and accounts enabled by Day 1 |
| Email & slack access | IT Ops | Can send and receive internal messages |
| System access (repos, CI) | Manager/EngOps | Able to clone, run tests, and open PRs |
| Benefits enrollment | People Ops | Completed within 30 days |
| Local compliance training | People Ops/Security | Completed within 14 days |

Role of the buddy:

- Provide social navigation for the first 30 days; shadow initial meetings; answer basic process questions. Not a technical mentor unless agreed.

4) Performance and feedback cycle

Cadence:
- Continuous feedback encouraged; use 1:1s weekly for early growth conversations.
- Formal review cycle: biannual performance reviews (mid-year and year-end) with calibration windows defined by People Ops.
- Promotion cycles: occur twice annually; managers submit promotion packets 4 weeks before calibration.

Manager responsibilities (high level):

- Provide clear goals and measurable success criteria (OKRs/SMART goals) within 30 days of hire or goal cycle start.
- Give regular, documented feedback; keep a record in the performance system (links in eng-developer-experience/docs-site).
- Complete interim check-ins (30/60/90), mid-year, and year-end reviews on time.
- Build a development plan for each direct report with measurable milestones.

Review process (step-by-step):

1. Self-assessment submitted by peer by due date (People Ops calendar).
2. Manager assessment completed with evidence snippets (projects, metrics, feedback).
3. Peer feedback solicited via standard template (anonymous where appropriate).
4. Calibration: managers present cases with evidence points to the calibration panel. Compensation recommendations are reviewed by Finance.

Performance rating scale (guidance):

- Exceeds Expectations (E): Sustained, high-impact contributions; consistently operates above role expectations.
- Meets Expectations (M): Delivers expected outcomes with growing independence.
- Developing (D): Partially meets expectations; needs targeted development.
- Unsatisfactory (U): Does not meet expectations; requires performance improvement plan.

Promotion guidelines:

- Promotions require evidence of impact, scope increase, and peer/manager corroboration. Use promotion packet template (linked in related_pages).
- Time-in-role expectations: typical minimum tenure: 12 months at IC levels, but exceptions exist for strong demonstrated impact.

5) Feedback culture and difficult conversations

- Managers should raise concerns early, document examples, and partner with People Ops for coaching.
- For performance improvement plans (PIPs): People Ops must be engaged before a PIP is issued. PIP duration is typically 60-90 days with clear success criteria.

6) Mobility, exits, and offboarding

- Internal mobility: encourage lateral and upward moves; manager to approve transfer plan and handover checklist.
- Voluntary exits: conduct exit interview (People Ops) and collect knowledge transfer notes.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke access within 24 hours of departure for privileged systems; remove from active oncall rotations and schedules. See security-and-compliance/incident-response-security for sensitive role handling.

Metrics and KPIs (People Ops dashboard):

- Time-to-offer (median): target <= 28 days.
- Time-to-fill (critical roles): target <= 45 days.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70%.
- New hire ramp (30/60/90): percent meeting defined 90-day success criteria: target >= 80%.
- Manager review completion rate (on-time): target >= 95%.

Templates and tools (where to find them)

- Interview scorecards, offer templates, and onboarding plans are in the Recruiting ATS and the People Ops Drive (links in eng-developer-experience/docs-site).
- Manager starter kit (checklists, goal templates, calibration slides) lives at /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops-manager-onboarding-feedback-and-performance-guide-2026.json.

Exceptions and escalation path

- Any deviations from the standard process (compensation, background checks, or onboarding windows) require written approval from the Head of People Ops and Legal where relevant.
- If hiring stalls >45 days for a critical role, the hiring manager must escalate to the People Ops director to re-evaluate sourcing and scope.

Appendices

A. Example 30/60/90 template (manager to fill):

- First 30 days: Learning goals, relationships to build, systems access, first deliverable description.
- Next 30 days (60): Increased responsibility, ownership of a medium-size task, initial performance metrics.
- Next 30 days (90): Full ownership of a recurring task or feature, mentoring a peer, and measurable impact.

B. Interviewer training checklist:

- Completed anti-bias training in last 18 months
- Reviewed role-specific rubric
- Read candidate's resume and prepared questions
- Committed to providing behaviorally specific feedback within 48 hours

C. Quick links & references:

- Benefits & enrollment portal: /confluence/company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks
- Data retention & PII policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/company-handbook/promotion-packet-template-2026

If you have questions or need an exception, contact people-ops@redwood.com.
